candidates.title: Diagnostic insights from twenty years of bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling for cushing disease at mayo clinic.
candidates.abstract: Bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling (BIPSS) is used to distinguish pituitary from ectopic sources of ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome (CS). We reviewed two decades of BIPSS experience at a single referral center to assess diagnostic performance, safety, and patient outcomes. Retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent BIPSS between 1998 and 2018. Of 156 adults undergoing BIPSS for ACTH-dependent CS, 143 had technically successful sampling and adequate follow-up and formed the evaluable cohort. A pituitary source was identified by a baseline central-to-peripheral ACTH ratio ≥2.0 or a post-stimulation (ovine corticotropin-releasing hormone [oCRH] or desmopressin) ratio ≥3.0. Diagnostic sensitivity, specificity, and lateralization accuracy of BIPSS. A confirmed pituitary source was defined by post-operative hypocortisolism after the index transsphenoidal operation; ACTH-positive corticotroph histology was supportive. Of the 143 patients, 109 had a definitive final diagnosis and formed the basis of the diagnostic analysis. BIPSS separated pituitary from ectopic ACTH sources with a sensitivity of 98.9% (95% CI 94.3-99.8) and a specificity of 85.7% (95% CI 60.1-96.0). The inter-petrosal gradient predicted the side of the adenoma in 59% of cases at baseline and 60% after stimulation (n = 100). Technical success was achieved in 94.2% of procedures, with no recorded major morbidity. Among the 94 patients in remission, 14 (15%) recurred over a mean of 3 years. Among patients in whom a definitive diagnosis was ultimately established, BIPSS distinguished pituitary from ectopic ACTH-dependent CS with high sensitivity and more modest specificity. Its value for adenoma lateralization is limited relative to current imaging. The cohort provides an oCRH-era reference point as practice moves to desmopressin.

candidates.title: Outcomes of Diabetic Macular Edema After Switching From Faricimab-svoa to High-dose Aflibercept.
candidates.abstract: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of high-dose aflibercept 8 mg in the treatment of diabetic macular edema (DME) refractory to faricimab-svoa treatment. This retrospective study included 82 eyes from 64 patients with DME previously treated with faricimab-svoa. Injection intervals, corrected or pinhole visual acuity (VA), and central foveal thickness (CFT) were recorded. Between the time of switch to the fifth injection, the average (SD) injection interval increased from 63 (45) days to 69 (23) days (P = .01). Mean VA decreased from 58.1 (23.1) to 52.9 (22.7) letters (P = .263), and average CFT decreased from 360 (145) µm to 348 (151) µm (P = .626). Intraretinal fluid incidence decreased from 50% to 33.3% (P = .066), while subretinal fluid incidence increased from 6.1% to 14.8% (P = .308). Anatomic and visual changes were not significant following switch to aflibercept 8 mg. Sustained injection interval improvements were present at the final aflibercept 8 mg injection.

candidates.title: Newly Diagnosed Graves' Disease Followed by the Discovery of a Cavernous Internal Carotid Artery Aneurysm Causing Panhypopituitarism: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Sellar and parasellar vascular lesions are rare causes of pituitary dysfunction and may mimic pituitary adenomas or other sellar masses. Cavernous internal carotid artery (ICA) aneurysms can cause hypopituitarism through compression of the pituitary gland or stalk, but diagnosis may be delayed when symptoms are initially attributed to a more common endocrine disorder. We report a 37-year-old man who presented with six weeks of unintentional weight loss, fatigue, heat intolerance, excessive sweating, anxiety, tremor, and tachycardia. Initial evaluation showed suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), elevated total triiodothyronine (T3), positive thyrotropin receptor antibody, positive thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin, and a hypervascular thyroid gland on ultrasound, consistent with Graves' disease. He was started on methimazole and atenolol. Although thyroid function tests improved, he developed persistent neck discomfort, prompting contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), which revealed an enhancing sellar mass. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed a T2-hypointense sellar lesion with internal flow artifact, and CT angiography confirmed a saccular aneurysm of the cavernous segment of the right ICA. Pituitary hormone evaluation demonstrated secondary adrenal insufficiency, central hypothyroidism, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, growth hormone (GH) deficiency, and mild hyperprolactinemia, consistent with panhypopituitarism from pituitary compression. The patient was started on prednisone and levothyroxine, and atenolol and prednisone were subsequently discontinued before endovascular embolization was performed. At follow-up, symptoms improved, but panhypopituitarism persisted. This case highlights the importance of reassessing patients when endocrine symptoms evolve despite an initially appropriate diagnosis.

candidates.title: Management of congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency: an update.
candidates.abstract: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) represents a group of autosomal recessive disorders characterized by enzyme deficiencies thatimpair adrenal steroidogenesis, most commonly due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency. The biochemical defects in CAH translate to a spectrumof clinical consequences, which include adrenal insufficiency, genital ambiguity or disordered sex development, infertility, short stature,and an increased risk of metabolic syndrome during adolescence and adulthood. The severity and clinical features of CAH vary dependingon the enzymatic defect, residual enzymatic activity, the age of presentation, and genotype. This review comprehensively covers the genetic background, classification, and clinical spectrum of CAH, including classical and non-classical forms. We discuss the importance and implementation of neonatal screening programs for early diagnosis and intervention. Specialattention is given to differences in treatment approaches between children and adolescents, highlighting the challenges of optimizingglucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid therapy across developmental stages. Furthermore, we present emerging novel pharmacologicalagents currently in clinical trials aimed at improving disease management. The review also addresses potential complications associatedwith CAH, such as metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular risks, and bone health issues. Emphasizing a patient-centered approach, wehighlight the critical role of experienced endocrinologists in delivering individualized care to improve long-term outcomes. Our review summarizes the current knowledge, aims to guide clinicians in evidence-based management and highlights ongoing research into innovativetherapies for CAH.

candidates.title: Personalised acromegaly treatment: implementing precision medicine in the Gulf States.
candidates.abstract: Acromegaly management in the Gulf region is complicated by a high burden of metabolic comorbidity, frequent presentation with macroadenomas and suboptimal biochemical control in available regional cohorts. Conventional first-generation somatostatin receptor ligands achieve biochemical control in only 30-40% of patients, rates lower than those observed in European cohorts, necessitating precision medicine strategies. MRI signal and tumour granulation patterns represent the most widely available biomarkers in Gulf healthcare systems and enable precise treatment selection. These biomarkers may help predict poor first-generation therapy response while identifying patients who may benefit from pasireotide, an efficacious second-generation somatostatin receptor ligand with multi-receptor binding capacity. Implementation of biomarker-guided therapy in Gulf healthcare systems can optimize therapeutic outcomes while addressing regional challenges of delayed diagnosis and advanced disease presentation. Regional challenges specific to Gulf healthcare systems are identified and a practical biomarker-guided algorithm tailored for the GCC region is proposed to optimise treatment selection using readily available diagnostic tools. This approach is more appropriate for Gulf populations who present with more advanced disease characteristics that may benefit from precision-guided first-line treatment selection, representing a paradigm shift away from current guideline recommendations toward truly personalised medicine. This evolution from empirical to precision medicine represents a potential advancement for improving acromegaly management where complex metabolic phenotypes demand sophisticated treatment strategies.

candidates.title: Acute Sheehan Syndrome Presenting as Panhypopituitarism and Reversible Cardiac Dysfunction in a Patient With Sickle Cell Disease: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Sheehan syndrome is an uncommon cause of hypopituitarism resulting from ischemic pituitary necrosis following severe postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) and hypotension. Its presentation can be delayed and non-specific, and it is rarely reported in the context of mild PPH with severe hemolysis. Here, we describe a 31-year-old woman with underlying sickle cell disease (SCD) who developed panhypopituitarism and reversible cardiac dysfunction after an 11-week period of progressive symptoms following spontaneous vaginal delivery complicated by an estimated blood loss of 700 mL and severe hemolysis. Pituitary hormonal replacement therapy, together with heart failure treatment, resulted in marked clinical and biochemical improvement, with normalization of metabolic abnormalities and recovery of cardiac function. This case suggests a possible association between Sheehan syndrome and postpartum blood loss of 700 mL accompanied by severe hemolysis, though this remains hypothetical based on a single case.

candidates.title: Association Between Trends in Geographic Atrophy Growth and Age-related Macular Degeneration Drusen Phenotype.
candidates.abstract: The purpose of this study was to characterize the association between geographic atrophy (GA) growth and age-related macular degeneration (AMD) drusen phenotype. This retrospective cohort study included 59 eyes from 47 patients over 55 years with GA, followed for up to 5 years. Eyes with poor-quality imaging, irregular follow-up, or exudation were excluded. Based on multimodal retinal imaging, eyes were classified into three groups: Group 1 (reticular pseudodrusen [RPD]), Group 2 (large soft drusen [LSD]), and Group 3 (mixed RPD and LSD). Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) images were analyzed from baseline to 60 months. GA lesion area and growth rate were measured semi-automatically using Region-Finder (Heidelberg Engineering) and compared across groups over time. The mean baseline GA area was 1.2 ± 0.8 mm2. The overall mean GA growth rate was 1.5 ± 0.9 mm2/year. Group 1 (RPD) showed the fastest progression at 2.56 ± 1.09 mm2/year, significantly higher than Group 2 (LSD, 1.02 ± 0.80 mm2/year) and Group 3 (1.10 ± 0.81 mm2/year) (P < .005). No significant difference was observed between Groups 2 and 3 (P = .28). These differences remained consistent at months 12, 24, 36, 48, and 60. GA progression is significantly faster in eyes with pure RPD phenotype. Mixed phenotype behaves similarly to LSD, supporting phenotype-specific monitoring and treatment strategies.

candidates.title: Improving Medication Safety for Patients with Adrenal Insufficiency Using Electronic Health Record Optimization.
candidates.abstract: Life-threatening adrenal crisis is preventable with timely administration of a stress dose of hydrocortisone, but recognition is often delayed. Sentinel patient safety events in 2020 highlighted the need to standardize adrenal insufficiency management. The primary aim of our quality improvement project was to reduce adrenal insufficiency medication errors in the emergency department (ED) by 10% from the baseline in 2 years. We included patients younger than 21 years with adrenal insufficiency and a prescription for parenteral hydrocortisone sodium succinate or oral hydrocortisone (prescribed by endocrinology) seen at our hospital between January 1, 2019, and September 30, 2023. Electronic health record (EHR) optimization changes included usage of a best practice advisory to improve visibility of adrenal insufficiency diagnosis and standardization of orders, steroid action plans, and education documentation. ED medication errors were defined as ED encounters with an emergency service index score of 1 or 2 with suboptimal stress dose (<50 mg/m2 of hydrocortisone sodium succinate) administration. The secondary outcome measure was safety reports related to medication errors in the ED or ambulatory setting. We analyzed outcome measures using statistical process control and tracked usage rates of EHR changes. We included 776 patients and 920 ED encounters. ED medication errors reduced from a baseline of 21% to 13.9% by study end. The interval between safety reports increased from an average of 74.4 to 775 days. Process measure use was 60% or greater for the problem list, best practice advisory, and steroid action plan, and 34% for education documentation. We successfully leveraged EHR optimization to standardize adrenal insufficiency management, increase visibility of critical information, and significantly reduce medication errors.

candidates.title: A case report of osilodrostat treatment in primary bilateral macronodular adrenal hyperplasia associated with bilateral adrenal mass reduction.
candidates.abstract: Primary bilateral macronodular adrenal hyperplasia (PBMAH) is a rare cause of Cushing syndrome (CS), characterized by bilateral adrenal nodules larger than 1 cm. Cortisol hypersecretion in PBMAH is driven by intra-adrenal rather than pituitary adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), with its pathogenesis mediated by aberrant hormone receptor expression in the adrenal cortex. This article reports a case of a 60-year-old woman with PBMAH in whom a marked reduction in bilateral adrenal masses was observed following treatment with osilodrostat. The patient presented with typical Cushingoid features, accompanied by hypertension, diabetes mellitus, osteoporosis, and severe restrictive lung disease. Genetic testing identified a pathogenic mutation in the ARMC5 gene, confirming the diagnosis. Because she was intolerant of surgical treatment, left adrenal artery embolization (AAE) was performed but failed to control hypercortisolism. Osilodrostat therapy was subsequently initiated-this potent 11β-hydroxylase inhibitor was recently approved in China for the treatment of Cushing syndrome. Notably, after 23 weeks of treatment, the patient's 24-hour urinary free cortisol (24 hours-UFC, CLIA) level returned to normal. Treatment was then discontinued, and during 11 months of follow-up the patient's 24 hours-UFC remained within the normal range. Moreover, imaging performed during the period of osilodrostat therapy demonstrated significant shrinkage of both adrenal glands. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of bilateral adrenal mass reduction observed in temporal association with osilodrostat treatment in a PBMAH patient. However, prior AAE confounds the attribution of tumor shrinkage to osilodrostat alone. These findings highlight an observed association between the drug and mass reduction, warranting further investigation to clarify its potential role beyond symptomatic control.

candidates.title: Beyond Digoxin Toxicity: A Fatal Case of BRASH Syndrome Triggered by Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
candidates.abstract: Bradycardia, renal failure, atrioventricular (AV) nodal blockade, shock, and hyperkalemia (BRASH) syndrome is a rare, life-threatening clinical condition caused by the synergistic interaction between hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction, and AV nodal blocking agents, resulting in severe bradycardia and hemodynamic instability. Early recognition is often challenging due to its nonspecific presentation. We report the case of an 82-year-old man with atrial fibrillation, ischemic heart disease, congestive cardiac failure, chronic kidney disease, and chronic digoxin therapy who presented with abdominal pain, confusion, dizziness, hypotension, and profound bradycardia. Investigations demonstrated severe hyperkalemia, acute kidney injury on top of chronic kidney disease, hyponatremia, and electrocardiographic changes consistent with hyperkalemia. Initial differential diagnoses included mesenteric ischemia, adrenal insufficiency, and digoxin toxicity; however, imaging excluded bowel ischemia, cortisol levels were normal, and serum digoxin at the therapeutic level. Community-acquired pneumonia complicated by sepsis was identified as the precipitating trigger for BRASH syndrome. Despite intensive treatment, including hyperkalemia management, isoprenaline infusion, antibiotics, corticosteroids, and supportive care, the patient's condition progressively deteriorated, culminating in multiorgan failure and death shortly afterward. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of BRASH syndrome and emphasizes the importance of early recognition and targeted management to interrupt the vicious cycle and improve clinical outcomes.

candidates.title: VIP-Mediated Syndromes: Contrasting Presentations and Multidisciplinary Management of Two Rare Neuroendocrine Tumors.
candidates.abstract: Vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP)-secreting tumors are rare neuroendocrine neoplasms that cause severe secretory diarrhea and electrolyte abnormalities. We describe 2 atypical cases requiring multidisciplinary care. One patient had a VIP-secreting pheochromocytoma with elevated VIP and metanephrine levels; symptoms improved after adrenalectomy. The second had a metastatic small intestinal neuroendocrine tumor with persistent VIP-mediated diarrhea despite debulking and somatostatin analog therapy, complicated by anal fissures, trans-sphincteric perianal fistula, and neuropathic pelvic pain. These cases highlight morbidity and potential complications associated with extrapancreatic VIP hypersecretion and the value of coordinated multidisciplinary management to improve outcomes and quality of life.

candidates.title: Enzalutamide alone or combined with other pharmacologic agents for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
candidates.abstract: BackgroundMetastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) remains driven by persistent androgen receptor signaling. Although enzalutamide (ENZ) is widely used, the incremental benefit of adding other agents remains uncertain. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of specific pharmacologic agents added to ENZ in randomized trials.MethodsWe systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Scopus through September 2026 following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420251231232). RCTs comparing ENZ plus another pharmacologic agent with ENZ monotherapy in mCRPC were included. Analyzed outcomes included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), radiographic PFS (rPFS), PSA progression, and adverse events. Random-effects meta-analyses used restricted maximum likelihood estimation with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE.ResultsNine trials involving 3779 patients were included. Adding specific agents to ENZ improved rPFS (HR = 0.76; 95% CI, 0.62-0.94; p = 0.02) but did not significantly improve OS, PFS, or PSA progression. Combination therapy increased the risk of any adverse event (RR = 1.03; 95% CI, 1.01-1.06) and grade ≥3 adverse events (RR = 1.37; 95% CI, 1.09-1.71). Estimates for individual adverse events were inconsistent and imprecise.ConclusionAdding specific agents to ENZ improved pooled rPFS but increased toxicity, without clear evidence of an OS benefit in unselected mCRPC populations (certainty of evidence ranging from very low to moderate across outcomes). These findings should be interpreted cautiously and do not exclude potential benefits from particular combinations in biomarker-selected populations.
candidates.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners

candidates.title: Upper Limb Neurorehabilitation Using a Hybrid Technology-Enabled Therapy Approach-A Scoping Review.
candidates.abstract: There is growing evidence of benefits for a multimodal or 'hybrid' technology approach where more than one technology type is applied for upper limb (UL) neurorehabilitation. However, translation of this approach into real world clinical settings remains unclear. Exploration of multimodal technology use for UL neurorehabilitation in hospital settings is warranted to determine practice trends, efficacy, benefits and barriers. A scoping review was conducted to explore hybrid technology-enabled rehabilitation approaches for UL neurorehabilitation focusing on combined use of robotics, virtual reality and sensor-based therapy. Seven electronic databases were searched for studies on adult participants with neurological UL impairment who participated in hospital rehabilitation and used two or more technology devices. Of 25 333 articles screened, full text review was completed on 20 articles with nine progressed for data extraction. An additional article found from hand searching was included for data extraction resulting in ten articles in total. Included studies found hybrid technology-enabled UL rehabilitation was used mainly with stroke participants ranging from 25 to 91 years in a hospital setting. Most studies were observational or pilot in nature and focused on clinical feasibility. All studies showed positive patient outcomes and feasibility studies reported on factors to support implementation in the clinical setting. Further research is warranted to determine impact on participation, long-term outcomes, sustainability, and economic impacts in the clinical hospital setting.

candidates.title: Pituitary Apoplexy Complicated by Pulmonary Embolism in a Neurologically Complex Patient: A Diagnostic Challenge.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary apoplexy is a rare endocrine emergency resulting from either acute haemorrhage or infarction within the pituitary gland. Although apoplexy occurs most frequently in a pre-existing pituitary adenoma, apoplexy could be the first presentation of a previously unknown adenoma. Acute headaches, visual disturbances, and neurological symptoms are common presenting symptoms in apoplexy; however, these symptoms may overlap with other neurological emergencies, which necessitate a holistic approach of clinical, radiological, and hormonal evaluation for suspected cases of apoplexy to confirm the diagnosis. Here we present a diagnostically challenging case of a 66-year-old man who presented with a sudden severe headache. His background history included a presumed intraventricular neurocytoma under surveillance. Initial CT head scan suggested possible haemorrhage within a known intraventricular mass (neurocytoma) with no obvious changes within the pituitary gland. However, subsequent MRI head demonstrated radiological features consistent with pituitary apoplexy. Later in his admission, he exhibited bilateral peripheral visual field constriction and early papilledema on fundoscopy. Hormonal testing showed evidence of hypopituitarism. The patient was managed conservatively with intravenous hydrocortisone replacement. During admission, he developed bilateral pulmonary emboli, for which he was treated with anticoagulation. While he was on anticoagulation, he developed intracranial haemorrhage, which led to his death after discharge from the hospital. This case demonstrates the importance of considering pituitary apoplexy in a challenging radiological and clinical presentation. A pre-existing neurological lesion (neurocytoma) makes a holistic approach, including MRI imaging and early hormonal evaluation are essential for timely diagnosis and treatment of pituitary apoplexy. The clinical challenge of having concurrent haemorrhagic and thrombotic events necessitates an individualised approach after balancing the benefits and risks of using anticoagulation treatment.

candidates.title: Sensitive detection of in vivo traumatic brain injury foci using magnetic particle imaging.
candidates.abstract: Diagnosing traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a major clinical challenge, particularly for mild to moderate cases, due to the limited sensitivity of conventional imaging modalities like magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) in detecting subtle cerebrovascular damage early after injury occurs. Magnetic particle imaging (MPI) is a novel modality that offers high sensitivity, linear quantification, and unambiguous detection of superparamagnetic tracers such as iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs). This study evaluates the capacity of MPI to detect and visualize cerebral bleeding resulting from TBI. A controlled cortical impact (CCI) closed-head TBI model was implemented using a calibrated electromagnetic impactor to induce moderate brain injury in C57BL/6 mice. IONPs were administered intravenously after impact, to mimic potential clinical use. CT-registered MPI images revealed strong, localized signals in the impact region of injured animals at early time points, while sham animals showed no residual signal in the brain. This localized signal decayed over time and eventually approached noise levels after 7 days post-injury. A direct comparison between MPI and -weighted MRI demonstrated that only MPI reliably differentiates the early injury foci at 24 hours. These results highlight the sensitivity and specificity of MPI as a potential diagnostic tool for detecting vascular disruption in TBI, offering a promising minimally invasive approach for early injury assessment. Additionally, these results demonstrate nanoparticle accumulation in sites of moderate TBI, highlighting potential theranostic applications of MPI to develop drug carriers suitable for treatment of TBI.

candidates.title: Proteomic profiling of somatotropinoma subtypes reveals TNIP1 overexpression in sparsely granulated tumors in a small discovery cohort.
candidates.abstract: The molecular mechanisms underlying the clinical differences between densely granulated (DG) and sparsely granulated (SG) somatotroph tumors remain poorly understood. To identify significant molecular differences between these subtypes, we performed quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomic profiling followed by validation of the differentially-identified proteins. Label-free quantitative proteomic analysis was performed on SG somatotroph adenomas (SGSAs, n = 3) and DG somatotroph adenomas (DGSAs, n = 3), with each sample analyzed in technical triplicate. Key findings were subsequently validated using immunohistochemistry (IHC, n = 64), immunofluorescence (IF, n = 24), and Western blotting (WB, n = 18). Proteomic profiling identified TNFAIP3-interacting protein 1 (TNIP1) as the most significantly over-expressed protein, and coenzyme Q6 monooxygenase (COQ6) as the most significantly under-expressed protein, in SGSAs compared with DGSAs. Higher TNIP1 expression in SGSAs was significantly associated with IGF-1 [%ULN], larger tumor diameter, greater tumor volume, higher Knosp grade and SSTR5 expression. In contrast, COQ6 expression showed significant negative correlations with tumor diameter, tumor volume, Knosp grade, and SSTR5 expression. These findings indicate strong associations between TNIP1 and COQ6 expression and tumor characteristics, along with differences in cell adhesion and signaling pathways. SGSAs and DGSAs exhibit distinct proteomic profiles. Increased TNIP1 and reduced COQ6 expression, together with alterations in cell adhesion and signaling pathways in SGSA, may contribute to the molecular and phenotypic differences underlying these somatotroph tumor subtypes.

candidates.title: Scleroderma-Like Phenotype in a Patient With Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis and Acromegaly: A Triple Diagnostic Challenge.
candidates.abstract: Systemic sclerosis, transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis, and acromegaly are rare disorders that share several clinical manifestations, including skin thickening, heart failure, dysphagia, fatigue, and soft tissue enlargement. Their coexistence is exceptionally rare and poses a significant diagnostic challenge, increasing the risk of premature diagnostic closure. We report a 78-year-old man who developed progressive diffuse skin thickening following spinal cord stimulator revision. Positive RNA polymerase III antibodies supported a diagnosis of diffuse systemic sclerosis. Evaluation of worsening edema and exertional dyspnea revealed severe concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with relative apical sparing on echocardiography, and technetium-99m pyrophosphate scintigraphy confirmed transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. Persistent macroglossia, coarse facial features, prior carpal tunnel syndrome, and a remote history of increasing ring and shoe size prompted endocrine evaluation, which demonstrated elevated insulin-like growth factor-1 levels, failure of growth hormone suppression, and a pituitary macroadenoma consistent with acromegaly. The patient underwent successful transsphenoidal resection with biochemical remission. This case highlights the importance of reconsidering the differential diagnosis when clinical features are not fully explained by an established diagnosis. Recognizing atypical and discordant findings prevented premature diagnostic closure and led to the identification of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis and acromegaly in a patient with a rapidly progressive scleroderma-like phenotype.

candidates.title: Beyond Accuracy: Inner Speech and Error Patterns Reveal Treatment-Based Learning in a Single-Subject Design Study.
candidates.abstract: In our recent single-subject design study, we showed that a sense of "successful inner speech (IS)" at baseline (i.e., "I can say it in my head") predicted treatment-related improvements in naming accuracy in four of five individuals with aphasia. Here, we analyze error patterns from those data to determine whether error patterns also changed after treatment and whether self-reported IS predicted such changes. Five adults with chronic poststroke aphasia completed 2 weeks of a cueing-based naming treatment targeting 40 personalized stimuli: 20 items reported prior to treatment as successful IS (sIS) and 20 items reported as unsuccessful IS (uIS). Before and after treatment, naming attempts were coded ordinally as follows: (0) no response, (1) neologism, (2) unrelated, (3) description, (4) semantic, (5) mixed, (6) phonological, and (7) correct. We used ordinal cumulative logit mixed-effects models to assess longitudinal changes in error types across all treatment items and in sIS versus uIS items. We evaluated individual-level changes by examining raw error type proportions across time. Naming performance improved from baseline testing to immediate posttreatment, when accounting for error types alongside naming accuracy. Participants' posttreatment naming attempts had higher odds of being closer to the target for sIS items versus uIS items, after controlling for baseline scores. Finally, most individual participants' error patterns changed across time, including one participant who was a "nonresponder" in our prior accuracy-based analysis. These preliminary findings suggest that error patterns are an important source of information about treatment-based learning in aphasia and converge with recent evidence that IS impacts naming treatment outcomes.

candidates.title: [Reference guide for the clinical management of adult Langerhans cell histiocytosis (key points from the first edition, 2025)].
candidates.abstract: According to the registry of the Japanese Society of Hematology, adult histiocytic neoplasms are extremely rare, with approximately 40 cases reported annually, and the most common among them is Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH). Lesions may involve multiple organs, including bone, skin, lung, the central nervous system, and the endocrine system. Without a hematology perspective, the neoplastic nature of LCH may not be apparent, resulting in missed diagnoses. Central diabetes insipidus, anterior pituitary dysfunction, and LCH-associated neurodegeneration, once developed, often result in irreversible impairment. Because delayed therapeutic intervention can result in permanent organ damage, it is essential for hematologists to understand the "minimum initial management" required to protect patient outcomes. This review summarizes the key points of diagnosis and initial management in adult LCH based on the first edition of the Adult LCH Clinical Reference Guide (2025).
candidates.journal: [Rinsho ketsueki] The Japanese journal of clinical hematology

candidates.title: Newborn Screening for X-Linked Adrenoleukodystrophy: A Systematic Literature Review.
candidates.abstract: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD) is the most common leukodystrophy and peroxisomal disorder. It was added to newborn screening (NBS) programs following its first implementation in New York in 2013. Since then, X-ALD screening has expanded rapidly, although important differences exist among programs. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the global implementation of NBS for X-ALD, including screening methodologies, screening performance, prevalence estimates, genetic findings, and clinical follow-up outcomes. A systematic search of PubMed and EMBASE identified 13 publications describing NBS programs conducted between 2013 and June 2026. All programs used C26:0-lysophosphatidylcholine (C26:0-LPC) as the primary biomarker, although substantial heterogeneity was observed in analytical methodologies, cut-off values, screening algorithms, and follow-up strategies. Positive predictive values ranged from 9.1% to 100%, while screening detection rates varied from 1:3118 to 1:51,081, reflecting differences in study design, screening population, sample size, and screening approaches. Variants of uncertain significance (VUS) accounted for 52.6% of individuals detected with classified ABCD1 variant findings, representing a major challenge for genetic counseling and clinical management. Most identified newborns were asymptomatic at diagnosis, supporting the role of NBS in enabling early surveillance for adrenal insufficiency and cerebral disease before irreversible manifestations occur. In addition, differences between universal and sex-specific screening strategies highlight ongoing clinical and ethical debates regarding the scope of X-ALD NBS. Overall, current evidence supports the feasibility of NBS for X-ALD and its ability to enable presymptomatic ascertainment and early clinical surveillance; however, greater harmonization of screening protocols, improved variant interpretation, and long-term outcome studies are needed to optimize program performance and clinical benefit.

candidates.title: AND-gate CRISPR/Cas13a-assisted colorimetric assay for dual microRNA monitoring of cervical spondylosis prognosis and auricular point pressing therapy evaluation.
candidates.abstract: Simultaneous detection of dual microRNA biomarkers is crucial for accurate prognosis and treatment monitoring of cervical spondylosis, yet remains challenging due to the lack of stringent logic control and high-fidelity signal amplification. Herein, we report an AND-gate-controlled colorimetric assay that integrates target-recycling strand displacement amplification, CRISPR/Cas13a/crRNA-mediated trans-cleavage, and self-priming cyclic amplification for sensitive and specific analysis of two cervical spondylosis-associated miRNAs (miRNA-221 and miRNA-146a). Only when both targets are present does the cascade proceed, producing double-stranded amplicons that trigger SYBR Green I-catalyzed TMB oxidation, yielding a naked-eye-visible blue signal. The assay exhibits a broad linear range from 10 fM to 500 pM, a detection limit of 2.12 fM, excellent selectivity, and good repeatability. Importantly, we applied this method to clinically evaluate the therapeutic effect of auricular point pressing (ear acupressure), a traditional Chinese medicine intervention for cervical spondylosis. In a 4-week study of 20 patients, the treatment group receiving auricular point pressing showed significant downregulation of both miRNAs compared to baseline, while the control group showed no notable change. Results correlated well with RT-qPCR, confirming reliability. This logic-controlled CRISPR/Cas13a platform offers a robust, equipment-free strategy for early prognosis of cervical spondylosis and objective monitoring of auricular point pressing therapy.
candidates.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications

candidates.title: Utility of the ACTH/cortisol ratio for differentiating pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas in dogs with pituitary-dependent hypercortisolism.
candidates.abstract: No simple, blood-based biomarker to estimate tumor size in dogs with pituitary-dependent hypercortisolism (PDH) has been evaluated. Determine whether the adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)/cortisol ratio differentiates pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas in dogs with PDH and correlates with pituitary size. Seventy privately-owned dogs with PDH (microadenomas, n = 30; macroadenomas, n = 40). Retrospective multicenter observational study. Endogenous ACTH and cortisol concentrations obtained at the same time point before treatment were used to calculate the ACTH/cortisol ratio. Pituitary tumor size was classified using the pituitary-to-brain (P/B) ratio. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and multivariable logistic regression. Dogs with macroadenomas had significantly higher ACTH/cortisol ratios than dogs with microadenomas (median, 9.12; IQR, 6.46-14.28 vs median, 4.90; IQR, 3.08-8.10; P < .001). The ratio showed moderate discrimination for differentiating macroadenomas from microadenomas with an area under the curve of 0.77 (95% CI, 0.66-0.89; P < .001). A cutoff >5.69 yielded 85% sensitivity and 60% specificity (positive likelihood ratio 2.13), whereas a higher ratio >11.74 achieved 90% specificity and 35% sensitivity (positive likelihood ratio 3.50). The ACTH/cortisol ratio showed moderate positive correlation with pituitary size (Spearman's ρ = 0.48; 95% CI, 0.26-0.64; P < .001) and remained independently associated with macroadenoma classification in multivariable analysis (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.05-1.40). The ACTH/cortisol ratio is associated with pituitary tumor size in dogs with PDH and may support clinical risk stratification, particularly when advanced imaging is unavailable.

candidates.title: Meaning of work: Perception of employment among veterans with substance use disorders.
candidates.abstract: BackgroundEmployment plays a significant role among veterans including facilitating their transition into the civilian society and is an important indicator of treatment progression for veterans presenting with substance use issues. While the Veterans Health Administration has instituted programs aimed at increasing employment outcomes among veterans, unemployment continues to be a significant problem among veterans presenting with substance use disorders (SUDs) in the United States.ObjectiveThe present study explored the perception and experience of work among veterans with a substance use history with a goal of understanding the complex meanings participants ascribe to employment.MethodsThe study utilized a qualitative research design. 25 veterans with self-identified history of substance use participated in the study.ResultsFour overarching themes were identified through thematic analysis: (a) source of economic support and independence, (b) provides structure, purpose and sense of accomplishment, (c) contribute to society and social connection, and (d) consequences of drug use on employment.ConclusionOverall, our findings indicate that despite the high unemployment rates among veterans with SUD, they are conscious of the benefits associated with being employed, which transcends the conventional role of employment as a mere source of income. Rehabilitation counselors and other professionals involved in the care for veterans with SUD should utilize an integrative treatment approach to care that includes employment as a critical component of recovery.

candidates.title: Pulmonary edema during cesarean delivery secondary to Takotsubo syndrome revealing pheochromocytoma: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Acute pulmonary edema during delivery is a serious condition with a wide range of etiologies, including Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), a form of transient left ventricular dysfunction most often presenting as apical ballooning. We report the case of a 35-year-old woman who developed severe hypertension (205/130 mmHg), polypnea, and a drop in oxygen saturation to 80% during cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia. She received noninvasive ventilation while the cesarean section continued and was transferred to the intensive care unit. Point-of-care ultrasound showed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35% with apical ballooning and diffuse B-lines on lung ultrasound. Computed tomography identified a right adrenal mass. A diagnosis of pulmonary edema complicating TTS was made, and the patient received furosemide and oxygen therapy. Further investigations, including urinary catecholamine metabolites, confirmed the diagnosis of pheochromocytoma. One week later, LVEF had recovered to 57% with mild residual apical hypokinesia and complete clinical recovery. The patient was then transferred to the surgical unit for management of the pheochromocytoma. This case demonstrates that TTS can cause pulmonary edema in the peripartum period, and that timely diagnosis is essential for a favorable outcome. Point-of-care ultrasound can be instrumental in guiding the assessment of such critical situations, and noninvasive ventilation may be of particular value in selected pregnant patients. This case also underscores the importance of an etiological workup and prompt treatment of hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, especially when pheochromocytoma is suspected, since anesthesia and surgery can precipitate decompensation.

candidates.title: Retinal Microvascular and Peripapillary Profiles in Mild Autonomous Cortisol Secretion Versus Nonfunctioning Adrenal Adenomas.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) is associated with increased cardiometabolic morbidity, but its relationship with the retinal microcirculation is unknown. We compared retinal and peripapillary microvascular parameters between MACS and nonfunctioning adrenal adenoma (NFA) and, secondarily, examined their associations with continuously modeled post-dexamethasone cortisol. Methods: In this single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study, 98 patients (45 NFA, 53 MACS) were included, and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) and structural OCT data from one eye per patient were analyzed. The primary outcome was whole-image deep capillary plexus (DCP) vessel density. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and cardiometabolic comorbidities; secondary analyses were corrected using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (q values). Results: OCTA was evaluable in 89 patients. The primary outcome did not differ significantly between groups in the main analysis (NFA vs. MACS, 48.64 ± 5.71% vs. 47.31 ± 5.77%; adjusted difference -1.29 percentage points, 95% CI -3.97 to 1.38; p = 0.339) or in any sensitivity analysis. In secondary analyses, superior retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness was greater in MACS (β = 17.38 µm; q < 0.001) and increased with ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) (β = 13.74 µm; q = 0.010). Higher ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) was also associated with lower parafoveal DCP (β = -2.72 percentage points; p = 0.013) and inside-disc radial peripapillary capillary vessel density (β = -3.13 percentage points; p = 0.026), which did not survive multiplicity correction; no superficial capillary plexus sector was associated with either exposure (all p ≥ 0.37). Conclusions: MACS was not significantly associated with whole-image DCP vessel density. The secondary associations with continuous cortisol are cross-sectional and hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation.

candidates.title: A Case of MEN 2A Syndrome With Bilateral Recurrent Pheochromocytoma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
candidates.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a neuroendocrine tumor arising from chromaffin cells and producing catecholamines. Due to the excessive release of catecholamines, these tumors can present with paroxysmal episodes of high blood pressure, headache, diaphoresis, and palpitations. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient who presented to the clinic with a history of headache, palpitations, and vomiting for two months. She was admitted for further investigations and management. Laboratory studies revealed elevated urinary and plasma catecholamine levels. Further work-up revealed bilateral adrenal masses diagnosed as pheochromocytoma and medullary thyroid cancer. The patient was diagnosed with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) type 2 and underwent bilateral laparoscopic adrenalectomy and total thyroidectomy with central and lateral neck dissection, and during surveillance, she was found to have recurrent pheochromocytoma. We also discuss the diagnosis and management of recurrent pheochromocytoma in MEN syndrome.

candidates.title: Non-Classical Apparent Mineralocorticoid Excess Syndrome: Current Evidence and Future Challenges.
candidates.abstract: Hypertension affects over 1.3 billion people worldwide and is the leading modifiable cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Approximately one-third of individuals with hypertension exhibit a low-renin phenotype, a clinically heterogeneous subgroup in whom the underlying etiology remains uncharacterized in most cases. Among its mechanistic contributors, non-classical apparent mineralocorticoid excess (NC-AME), defined by partial insufficiency of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 (11β-HSD2), represents a prevalent and underrecognized cause of cortisol-mediated mineralocorticoid receptor overactivation that has, to date, lacked a formal clinical definition, standardized diagnostic criteria, or evidence-based therapeutic framework. This Scientific Statement addresses that gap. The panel formally defines NC-AME as a syndrome of partial 11β-HSD2 insufficiency occurring in the absence of biallelic HSD11B2 variants, biochemically characterized by an elevated cortisol-to-cortisone (F/E) ratio and low cortisone concentration, and typically associated with low plasma renin, normal-to-low aldosterone, and elevated blood pressure. The Statement consolidates evidence across three mechanistic domains, genetic and epigenetic dysregulation of HSD11B2, endogenous and exogenous enzyme inhibition, and patient-specific alterations (i.e. age, sex, renal function), and proposes both a structured, an LC-MS/MS-based diagnostic algorithm, and a resource-adapted diagnostic approach. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists are endorsed as mechanism-directed first-line therapy, with blood pressure and renin normalization as co-primary treatment targets. Acquired and reversible causes are classified separately to guide clinical management. A research agenda is advanced to drive threshold standardization, multicenter validation, and integration of NC-AME into hypertension guidelines across endocrinology, cardiology, and nephrology.
